slides.title: Why Katalyst exists — Aaron's expanded thesis (v2)
slides.subtitle: Cadence-direction matrix · cost-buffer collapse · authority outside the harness · three taxonomy pillars
slides.notes: Hand-authored canonical reference for what Katalyst is for. 'Fast in the wrong direction is worse than slow.' The cadence-direction matrix names the danger zone (fast-wrong, agentic alone), the target state (fast-right, Katalyst), the pre-AI slow-but-filtered state, and the post-AI cheap-and-unfiltered state. The pre-AI cost-of-features acted as a buffer that filtered out wrong-direction work; AI removed the cost, the filter is gone, Katalyst's taxonomy replaces it. Authority lives outside the developer harness — Product Owner, HCD/UX, Architect, Mission Owner are sources of authoritative judgment. Three taxonomy pillars: Need, Design Intent, Implementation Reality — with acknowledged GAP that visual design intent has no Forge artifact yet.

slides.title: RIC-401 — The 3-loop design process
slides.subtitle: outer (quarters→years) · inner (days→weeks) · hypothesis (always-on)
slides.notes:
Three loops, three cadences, three authority sets.

Outer loop (cadence: quarters → years; authority: leadership + mission stakeholder): vision → need → design system → design intent. Direction gets set here.

Inner loop (cadence: days → weeks; authority: PM + HCD + UX + Eng + architect): frame → IA → wireframes → mockups → validation → build/ship → design QA. The per-feature design iteration. HCD/UX is irreplaceable — AI cannot synthesize visual design intent.

Hypothesis loop (cadence: always-on; authority: PM + Research + Data): hypothesis statement → success metrics + kill criteria → telemetry → outcome (CONFIRMED / REFUTED / PARTIAL). Real user data is the only thing that can answer the hypothesis.

Pattern extraction (orange thick arrow) flows CONFIRMED outcomes back into the Outer Design System — the load-bearing connection.

slides.title: Katalyst taxonomy — artifact dependencies
slides.subtitle: Three pillars · cross-pillar refs labeled with frontmatter field names
slides.notes:
Dependency graph of artifact types in the Katalyst taxonomy, organized by Aaron's three pillars.

NEED lane (orange): organization.yaml, user_types/, user_stories/, environments.yaml.
DESIGN INTENT lane (blue): design/adr/, design/nfr/, design/specifications/, taxonomy.lock.
IMPLEMENTATION REALITY lane (green): actions/just/, layerTypes/, cicd/templates/, code · running systems.

Arrows are labeled with the actual metadata field names that create the link: user_type_ref, related_adrs, related_user_types, stories[], environments[]. Bottom-left callout names the GAP from Aaron's v2 thesis (visual design intent has no Forge artifact yet); bottom-right explains how the dependency graph enforces value-proof traceability at runtime.

slides.title: Why Katalyst exists — plugin-rendered v1
slides.subtitle: Same argument as slide 1, this time generated by the plugin (proof the renderer handles real conceptual content)
slides.notes:
The plugin's take on the same thesis Aaron hand-authored in slide 1. Software only matters if it can prove its value. SaaS proves value via usage because users have AGENCY. Enterprise / government has no agency — usage proves nothing. Value must be DESCRIBED. Historically descriptions happen at human speed; agents work at agent speed; gap widens; value-proof fails. Katalyst surfaces value at agent speed via the three-pillar taxonomy.

Simpler than the v2 — same core argument without the cadence-direction matrix or the cost-buffer framing. Captured here as proof the plugin can render real conceptual content from a structured spec, not just code-derived diagrams.
